title: Set up a capability
summary: Settings lists the capabilities installed with the server. You switch Reports on and connect GitHub: the server gives a code, you approve it on GitHub, where you're already signed in, and GitHub hands the token to the server, which turns Reports on. The token never reaches the app, only that one is set.

capabilities.title: Reports
capabilities.summary: Takes your feedback, and what Ari couldn't do, to Ito's developers as public GitHub issues.

fields.name: token
fields.title: GitHub token
fields.description: Connect GitHub, so Reports files issues on akai-ito/ito-core as you.

capabilities.title: iCloud
capabilities.summary: Your iCloud Mail and Calendar, read and kept by Kumo on your box.

fields.name: apple_id
fields.title: Apple ID
fields.description: The email address you sign in to iCloud with.

fields.name: app_password
fields.title: App-specific password
fields.description:
Apple has no sign-in for other apps, so Kumo uses an app-specific password.
1. Open Apple Account and sign in.
2. In Sign-In and Security, choose App-Specific Passwords.
3. Add one called Ito, and paste it here.

It goes to your box only. One connection covers Mail and Calendar.

capabilities.title: Outlook
capabilities.summary: Your Outlook.com mail, read by Kumo on your box. Kumo writes drafts and never sends.

fields.name: token
fields.title: Microsoft account
fields.description:
Sign in with Microsoft so Kumo can read your Outlook.com mail.
1. Open Microsoft and enter the code.
2. Sign in, and allow access to your mail.

The box keeps the sign-in and renews it itself.

capabilities.title: Gmail
capabilities.summary: Your Gmail, read by Kumo on your box. Kumo writes drafts and never sends.

fields.name: app_password
fields.title: App password
fields.description:
Gmail lets other apps in with an app password, once 2-Step Verification is on.
1. Open Google App Passwords and sign in.
2. Make one called Ito.
3. Paste the 16 letters here.

It goes to your box only.
